citation.title: Measurements of the fast ion slowing-down times in the HL-2A tokamak and comparison to classical theory
citation.authors: Y. P. Zhang, M. Isobe, Yi Liu, G. L. Yuan, J. W. Yang, et al. (HL-2A Team)

topic: Neutral-beam blip fast-ion slowing-down times on HL-2A, inferred from fission-chamber D-D neutron decay and compared with a classical Spitzer-based model.
own_question: Do beam-injected fast deuterons slow down classically without significant loss under ohmic and ECRH conditions with varying Te and ne?
actual_method_and_evidence: 5 ms, 0.8 MW co-injected D beam blips. Neutron e-folding decay times were measured, e.g. about 13.1 ms ohmic and about 16.7 ms ECRH. They were compared with a classical slowing-down estimate whose Ti profile was assumed equal to Te. The source reports agreement near the core without ECRH. With ECRH, it reports a discrepancy that the authors attribute to Ti being lower than Te. Trends versus ne and Te are shown statistically.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. There is no CES, BES, ECEI, causal estimation, or nowcasting; the analysis is offline.
validation_if_relevant: No predictive validation design or data split.
forbidden_inferences: Any statement about CES impurity Ti, its timing, or its nowcastability
Treating the source's assumption that Ti equals Te as measured Ti
Generalizing an HL-2A fast-ion result to KSTAR pedestal ion temperature
Using it as evidence about fluctuation diagnostics or real-time control
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The topic is fast-ion slowing down measured with neutrons, which is unrelated to causal nowcasting of reported pedestal-top CES temperature. Its only tangential point is the authors' statement that ECRH raised Te far more than Ti. That is a single-shot remark, not a measurement useful to our study.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
